neighbours.label: In English, the subject (strongest when it is a pronoun) that opens a purpose clause introduced by 'so', 'so that' or 'in order that', just before its can/could/would; quiet for a result 'so' after a comma, for degree 'so', and for clauses after 'because' or 'in case'.
fire: She left the porch light on so that he could find the house in the dark.
Speak slowly so they can follow every step of the recipe.
We packed extra sandwiches so we would not have to stop on the highway.
The teacher wrote the answers on the board so that everyone could check their work.
I saved a little each month in order that I could buy a bicycle by summer.
He lowered the shelf so she could reach the cereal without a stool.
Leave the door unlocked so that I can get in after my shift.
They built a ramp beside the stairs so it would be easier for wheelchairs.
quiet: She left the porch light on, so he found the house easily in the dark.
Speak slowly because they are still learning the language.
We packed extra sandwiches in case we got hungry on the highway.
The teacher was so tired that she forgot to write the answers on the board.
I saved a little each month, so I bought a bicycle by summer.
He lowered the shelf because she could not reach the cereal.
Leave the door unlocked in case I come home after my shift.
The ramp beside the stairs was so steep that nobody used it.
